string.text: Do not hoard everything you find in the zone. As a rule, things found in the zone, such as artifacts, weapons, and food can be contaminated with radiation. To check if an item is contaminated with radiation, highlight it with your curser; Messer's geiger counter will tick if the item in question is contaminated. These contaminated items will emit radiation even if they are stored in the backpack, slowly irradiating its bearer.
To crouch, press ($$ACTION_crouch$$). To crouch even lower, press ($$ACTION_crouch$$) + ($$ACTION_accel$$)
Some stalkers will refuse to talk to you if you stick your weapon in their face. To hide your weapon, pull out a bolt. ($$ACTION_wpn_6$$).
Jumping will help you climb onto, or over objects. To jump, press ($$ACTION_jump$$)

You're not a mule, so there's a limit to how much you can carry. When the weight of your gear exceeds your limits, you will start losing energy very quickly. You can monitor the current weight of your equipment and the maximum weight you can carry in your inventory.

When the Messer wears a radioactive artifact on his belt or enters an area with a high level of background radiation, he starts losing health and exhibits signs of radiation poisoning. The effects of radiation poisoning can be countered by using antiradiation drugs and vodka.

By helping other characters, you improve their attitude towards you. This will also improve your general reputation. Better attitude and higher reputation help you when interacting with the people you meet. If they view you positively, they will be amenable to discounted trading and will offer additional information. On the other hand, if you attack someone, their attitude towards you will instantly turn negative, as will that of their friends, and they will attack you.

This is a good place to hit the sack. Here you can get a good night's sleep, wait out the night, or simply kill some time. To go to sleep, open the Inventory, set the amount of time you want to sleep and press the Rest button. Messer will wake up at the designated time. Sometimes, he will have dreams.

Sometimes you will need to sprint for one reason or another. To do this, press ($$ACTION_sprint_toggle$$) while running. Sprinting will cause Messer to run faster and jump farther, but he will tire more quickly and will be unable to shoot his gun.

If Messer does not eat for a while, he becomes hungry. Unless he finds something to eat, he will start losing health. To prevent this, Messer must eat regularly. A loaf of bread, tinned food, or a piece of sausage will satisfy his hunger, at least for a while.

Running for a prolonged period of time causes fatigue. When Messer becomes exhausted, he will not be able to run and will move at walking pace. The more weight Messer carries in his inventory, the faster his stamina drains. Standing still for a moment is enough to recuperate stamina.

All weapons have a durability parameter. The lower a weapon's durability, the more often it jams. To unjam, reload the weapon by pressing $$ACTION_wpn_reload$$. The weapon's durability decreases with use. If a weapon is struck by gunfire, it will be likely be rendered inoperable.

When Messer is hit, he may start to bleed. This will cause him to constantly lose health. The more serious the bleeding, the faster the rate at which Messer loses health. A green icon means minor bleeding, and a red icon indicates a serious hemorrhage. Bleeding will eventually stop with time, and even serious hemorrhages can be stopped immediately by using bandages.

Exoskeletons rely on a specialized battery pack for a full range of motion. A depleted exoskeleton imposes penalties on movement speed, so it must be charged to be used effectively. Additionally, a charged exoskeleton enables you to sprint while wielding a Gauss Rifle. The exoskeleton or its battery pack can be recharged at the scientists' base. \n \nTo insert the battery pack into the the exoskeleton, drag the battery pack onto its icon, or right-click the battery pack. The battery pack can be removed by right-clicking on the exoskeleton.
Anomaly detectors worn on the belt slowly drain the device's battery. To replace the detector's battery, drag a fresh battery onto its icon.
